description: Complete CreatorOS data model: every table, column, relationship, constraint, enum, and migration path from schema.ts plus all missing tables required by desired state (16 modules, 10 product types, full commerce/UGC/ads/automation stack).

schema_surfaces.summary: CreatorOS data lives in a single schema surface (shared/schema.ts) with a Python projection integration layer in UMH. Unlike EOS, there is no Beast divergence — GitHub main and Beast are aligned.

surfaces.pk_strategy: serial (auto-increment integer) for all tables except notifications (uuid)
surfaces.critical_vuln: comparePasswords returns true for ALL passwords in dev mode — any password works for any user

surfaces.note: Read/write typed Python wrappers over the same Neon tables defined in schema.ts. Single coupling point between UMH substrate and CreatorOS data.

current_tables.name: users
current_tables.description: Core user identity. Serves both creator and consumer roles via text role field. Central entity all other tables FK to.

relationships.note: notifications where this user is the actor

current_tables.design_notes: No email field. No OAuth fields. No email verification. Role is a free-text field with no enum constraint. XP/level system exists but no corresponding XP-earning logic found in codebase.

current_tables.name: posts
current_tables.description: Content posts supporting multiple media types (text, photo, audio, video). Denormalized like/comment counts. No cross-posting metadata, no scheduling fields, no platform targeting.
current_tables.design_notes: likes and comments are denormalized counters (not derived from joins). media_type is nullable despite the schema comment suggesting text/photo/audio/video enum. No published_at, scheduled_at, or status field. No platform targeting for cross-posting.

current_tables.name: saved_posts
current_tables.description: Junction table for user bookmarks/saves of posts.

current_tables.name: comments
current_tables.description: Threaded comments on posts. Self-referential parent_id for nested replies.
current_tables.design_notes: parent_id has no formal FK constraint in the pgTable definition (just an integer column), but Drizzle relations define parent/replies self-referential relationship. likes is a denormalized counter.

current_tables.name: products
current_tables.description: Creator products for marketplace. Generic product table with no product type discriminator. No price variants, no inventory, no digital delivery, no checkout flow.
current_tables.design_notes: No product_type discriminator column for the 10 product types defined in PRD. No stripe_product_id, no status field, no published/draft states. rating and review_count are denormalized but no reviews table exists. price is doublePrecision (float) instead of numeric/decimal — problematic for currency. category is free text, not enum. No relationship to orders or entitlements (neither table exists).

current_tables.name: ai_agents
current_tables.description: Creator-configured AI agents with customizable persona, system prompt, and visual appearance. Uses OpenAI SDK.
current_tables.design_notes: status is free text (no enum). chat_count is denormalized. No token usage tracking, no model selection field, no pricing/billing for AI usage.

current_tables.name: ai_chats
current_tables.description: Chat sessions between users and AI agents. Messages stored as JSON blob rather than individual message rows.
current_tables.design_notes: messages is a JSON blob — not queryable, not indexable, no per-message metadata. No title/summary field for chat sessions.

current_tables.name: communities
current_tables.description: Discord-like community spaces. Notably has NO owner/creator FK — communities are ownerless in the schema.
current_tables.design_notes: CRITICAL GAP: No owner_user_id FK. No membership table (community_members). No privacy/visibility field. No slug for URL routing. No icon_url (only icon_color). No category or type field. The PRD describes communities as creator-owned with membership tiers and access gating — none of that is modeled.

current_tables.name: channels
current_tables.description: Text channels within communities (Discord channel model).
current_tables.design_notes: No channel type (text/voice/video/announcement). No topic/description. No position/order field. No permissions or role-gating.

current_tables.name: channel_messages
current_tables.description: Messages within community channels.
current_tables.design_notes: No media attachment support. No reactions (unlike direct_messages which have reactions JSON). No threading/reply support. No edit history.

current_tables.name: followers
current_tables.description: User-to-user follow relationships. Bidirectional via two FK columns to users.

current_tables.name: revenue
current_tables.description: Revenue tracking entries for creator dashboard. Manual/seeded revenue records — not tied to an orders or transactions table.
current_tables.design_notes: amount is doublePrecision (float) — problematic for currency. source is free text. No FK to orders, products, or transactions. No currency field. This table appears designed for dashboard visualization only, not actual commerce.

current_tables.name: contacts
current_tables.description: Basic CRM contacts for creators to track their customers/audience members.
current_tables.design_notes: Minimal CRM. purchase_info is free text, not structured. No email field on contacts. No link to user accounts (contacts are not necessarily platform users). No tags, segments, or lifecycle stage.

current_tables.name: documents
current_tables.description: Notion-style rich text documents for creators.
current_tables.design_notes: content is plain text — no structured block editor format. No sharing/collaboration fields. No folder/hierarchy. Not mentioned in PRD — appears to be an implementation addition.

current_tables.name: stories
current_tables.description: 24-hour ephemeral stories (Instagram/Snapchat model) with view counting.
current_tables.design_notes: expires_at is nullable — no automatic enforcement of 24h expiry. view_count is denormalized (no story_views table to track who viewed). media_type defaults to 'image' — supports image/video per schema comment.

current_tables.name: notifications
current_tables.description: User notification feed. Only table using UUID primary key (all others use serial).

relationships.note: the user who triggered the notification

current_tables.design_notes: related_user_image is denormalized (duplicates profile_image_url from users). type is free text, not enum. Only table with UUID PK — inconsistent with the rest of the schema. related_user_id FK has no ON DELETE behavior specified.

current_tables.name: conversations
current_tables.description: DM conversation containers supporting both 1:1 and group chats.

current_tables.name: conversation_participants
current_tables.description: Junction table linking users to conversations. Supports admin designation for group chats.

current_tables.name: direct_messages
current_tables.description: Individual messages within conversations. Supports replies, edit tracking, and emoji reactions.

columns.name: reply_to_message_id
constraints: self-referential FK (defined in relations, not in column)

current_tables.design_notes: is_edited is nullable boolean (inconsistent — should be NOT NULL with default false). reactions is a JSON blob {userId: reactionType}. No media attachment support. read is per-message, not per-participant (problematic for group chats).

current_tables.name: tagged_users
current_tables.description: Users tagged at specific positions within image/media posts.
current_tables.design_notes: Position-based tagging for Instagram-style photo tags. The unique constraint includes position coordinates, so a user CAN be tagged multiple times on the same post at different positions.

missing_tables.name: businesses
missing_tables.description: Creator business entity — the organizational unit that owns products, communities, and commerce. Maps to the PRD concept of a creator's 'store' or 'business'.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD primitive chain is User -> CreatorAccount -> Business -> Product -> Order -> Entitlement. Currently users directly own products. A business entity enables multi-creator businesses, team permissions, Stripe Connect per-business, and proper tax/legal separation.

columns.name: transaction_fee_pct
columns.note: Platform fee percentage based on tier

missing_tables.name: business_members
missing_tables.description: Team members of a business with role-based access. Enables multi-person creator businesses.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD specifies Roles & Permissions module. Business tier includes team seats. Without business_members, there is no multi-user business support.

missing_tables.name: connected_accounts
missing_tables.description: OAuth connections to external platforms (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Twitter, etc.) for cross-posting and analytics.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD modules 1 (Content Distribution), 10 (Cross-Posting), and Connected Accounts screen all require platform connections. Core to the 'post once, publish everywhere' promise. No current schema support.

columns.name: platform
columns.note: youtube | instagram | tiktok | twitter | facebook | twitch | linkedin | spotify

missing_tables.name: orders
missing_tables.description: Purchase orders for any product type. Central commerce record linking buyer, product, and payment.
missing_tables.rationale: Products table exists but there is no way to purchase anything. PRD primitive chain requires Order. No checkout, no payment, no purchase history without this table.

columns.name: amount_cents
columns.note: Price in cents to avoid float precision issues

missing_tables.name: transactions
missing_tables.description: Financial ledger entries for payouts, fees, and refunds. Feeds the revenue dashboard with real data instead of seeded records.
missing_tables.rationale: Revenue table is manually seeded data for dashboard visualization. Real commerce needs a proper transaction ledger tied to orders and Stripe events.

missing_tables.name: entitlements
missing_tables.description: Access grants that result from completed orders. Controls what a buyer can access (course enrollment, community membership, software access, etc.).
missing_tables.rationale: PRD primitive chain ends with Entitlement. Without entitlements, purchased products grant no actual access. Required for courses, memberships, software access, and gated communities.

columns.name: type
columns.note: course_access | community_access | download_access | subscription | software_access | event_ticket | service_booking

missing_tables.name: courses
missing_tables.description: Online course container with pricing, enrollment tracking, and curriculum structure.
missing_tables.rationale: Course Platform is module 3 of 16 in the PRD. Products table has no course-specific fields (curriculum, progress, drip). Courses need dedicated modeling for the Teachable-like experience described in the PRD.

missing_tables.name: lessons
missing_tables.description: Individual lessons within a course. Supports video, text, quiz, and assignment content types.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD describes drag-and-drop course builder with video hosting, progress tracking, and quizzes. Lessons are the atomic unit of course content.

columns.name: drip_delay_days
columns.note: Days after enrollment before lesson unlocks

missing_tables.name: enrollments
missing_tables.description: Student enrollment in courses with progress tracking. Links to entitlements for access control.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD describes My Courses screen with progress indicators and Course Player with progress tracking. Without enrollments, there is no course completion tracking.

missing_tables.name: lesson_completions
missing_tables.description: Tracks which lessons each student has completed. Granular progress below enrollment level.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD describes per-lesson progress tracking. enrollment.completed_lessons is a denormalized counter — this table provides the source of truth.

missing_tables.name: community_members
missing_tables.description: Membership tracking for communities with role-based access and tier gating.
missing_tables.rationale: Communities table has no owner FK and no membership table. PRD describes free/paid community tiers with membership gating. Without this table, communities have no members.

missing_tables.name: ugc_campaigns
missing_tables.description: UGC (User-Generated Content) campaign listings created by businesses to recruit creators.
missing_tables.rationale: UGC Campaigns is module 8 of 16 in the PRD. PRD describes full UGC workflow: create listing, review applicants, approve deliverables, pay. No schema support exists.

columns.name: requirements
columns.note: Content requirements, platform targets, audience minimums

missing_tables.name: ugc_applications
missing_tables.description: Creator applications to participate in UGC campaigns.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD UGC workflow includes review applicants step. Applications are the junction between creators and campaigns.

missing_tables.name: ugc_deliverables
missing_tables.description: Content deliverables submitted by accepted UGC creators for campaign review and approval.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD UGC workflow includes approve deliverables and pay steps. Deliverables track the actual content submitted for a campaign.

missing_tables.name: ad_campaigns
missing_tables.description: Advertiser campaigns with targeting, budgets, and bidding. Self-serve ads platform (YouTube/Meta-like).
missing_tables.rationale: Ads Platform is module 9 of 16 in the PRD. PRD describes Ad Campaign Manager screen with targeting, budgets, and metrics. No schema support exists.

columns.name: targeting
columns.note: Audience targeting criteria: demographics, interests, locations

missing_tables.name: ads
missing_tables.description: Individual ad creatives within a campaign. Each ad has its own creative content and performance metrics.
missing_tables.rationale: Ad campaigns contain multiple ad variations for A/B testing and creative rotation. Performance tracked per-ad.

missing_tables.name: automations
missing_tables.description: Visual automation workflows (Manychat-style) with trigger/action chains.
missing_tables.rationale: Automation Builder is module 11 of 16 in the PRD. PRD describes visual flow builder for trigger/action automations covering commerce, community, and email. No schema support exists.

columns.name: flow_definition
columns.note: Serialized visual flow graph: nodes (triggers, conditions, actions) and edges

missing_tables.name: automation_runs
missing_tables.description: Execution log for automation triggers. Tracks each time an automation fires, what it did, and whether it succeeded.
missing_tables.rationale: Automations need execution history for debugging, analytics, and audit. Without a runs table, there is no visibility into automation behavior.

columns.name: trigger_event
columns.note: The event payload that triggered this run

missing_tables.name: email_lists
missing_tables.description: Email subscriber lists for newsletter/broadcast management.
missing_tables.rationale: Email/Newsletter is module 12 of 16 in the PRD. PRD describes list management and templates. No schema support exists.

missing_tables.name: subscribers
missing_tables.description: Email subscribers on a list. Can be platform users or external email-only subscribers.
missing_tables.rationale: Email lists need subscribers. Subscribers may be platform users or external emails captured via landing pages.

missing_tables.name: broadcasts
missing_tables.description: Email broadcasts/newsletters sent to subscriber lists.
missing_tables.rationale: PRD describes email broadcasts with templates. Broadcasts are the actual emails sent to lists.

missing_tables.name: reviews
missing_tables.description: User reviews and ratings for products. Source of truth for denormalized rating/review_count on products table.
missing_tables.rationale: Products table has rating and review_count columns but no reviews table. These denormalized fields have no source of truth. Marketplace requires user reviews for trust.

missing_tables.name: categories
missing_tables.description: Product and content categories for marketplace discovery and filtering.
missing_tables.rationale: Products.category is a free-text field. PRD describes marketplace with filters by type, price, category. Structured categories enable consistent filtering and discovery.

missing_tables.name: post_platforms
missing_tables.description: Cross-posting tracking. Records which platforms a post was published to and its per-platform status/metrics.
missing_tables.rationale: Core to the 'post once, publish everywhere' promise. Without per-platform tracking, there is no cross-posting analytics, no per-platform status, and no way to know where a post was distributed.

columns.name: platform_post_id
columns.note: The ID of the post on the external platform

missing_tables.name: moderation_actions
missing_tables.description: Content moderation log for trust and safety compliance.
missing_tables.rationale: Moderation, Trust & Safety, Compliance is module 15 of 16 in the PRD. PRD describes moderation suite with auto-mod and appeals. No schema support exists.

columns.name: target_id
columns.note: Polymorphic ID of the moderated entity

columns.name: action
columns.note: warn | remove | ban | mute | flag | approve

enums.note: CreatorOS uses free-text columns for all enum-like values. No Drizzle pgEnum declarations exist in schema.ts. These are the de facto value sets inferred from code defaults and PRD specifications.

values.name: user_role
values.enforcement: none — free text field with default 'creator'
values.note: PRD also describes 'advertiser' role but not in current schema

values.name: post_media_type
values.enforcement: none — free text field with default 'text'

values.name: story_media_type
values.enforcement: none — free text field with default 'image'

values.name: ai_agent_status
values.enforcement: none — free text field with default 'active'
values.note: Only 'active' default defined; presumably 'inactive', 'archived' exist but are not specified

values.name: notification_type
values.enforcement: none — free text field, no default
values.note: Values inferred from typical social platform notification types; not explicitly defined in schema

values.name: product_type
values.note: Products table has no type discriminator. All 10 types would share the same products table with a type column + type-specific extension tables (courses, etc.)

values.name: platform
values.column: N/A — missing from schema (needed for connected_accounts)

values.name: order_status
values.column: N/A — missing from schema (needed for orders table)

values.name: entitlement_type
values.column: N/A — missing from schema (needed for entitlements table)

values.name: business_member_role
values.column: N/A — missing from schema (needed for business_members table)

values.name: community_member_role
values.column: N/A — missing from schema (needed for community_members table)

primitive_chain.current_implementation: User -> Product (direct FK, no Business layer, no Order, no Entitlement)

gap_analysis.CreatorAccount_Business: MISSING — no businesses table. users.role='creator' is the only creator distinction. No Stripe Connect, no team seats, no business profile.
gap_analysis.Product: PARTIAL — products table exists but lacks type discriminator, status field, Stripe product ID, and variant support
gap_analysis.Order: MISSING — no orders table. No purchase flow, no checkout, no payment records.
gap_analysis.Entitlement: MISSING — no entitlements table. Purchased products grant no access. No course enrollment gating, no community membership gating, no download delivery.

rls.current_state: No Row-Level Security policies exist. All data access is server-side via Express routes with Passport.js session auth. No Neon RLS, no Postgres RLS policies.
rls.target: user_id or business_id scoped RLS policies
migration_notes: Moving to Clerk auth will change the auth model entirely — session-based to JWT-based
RLS policies should scope to business_id for creator data (products, orders, revenue, courses, campaigns) and user_id for consumer data (enrollments, saved posts, follows)
Multi-tenant: each business is a tenant boundary for creator-side data
Consumer data (follows, saves, enrollments) is scoped to user_id regardless of business

migration_path.description: Migration from current 20-table schema to full desired-state schema. Ordered by dependency (leaf tables first, junction tables after parents).

changes: Add email column to users table (currently missing)
Add clerk_id column to users table
Remove password column after Clerk migration
Fix comparePasswords security vulnerability by removing dev-mode bypass entirely
phases.open_question: Clerk migration timing: before or after commerce tables? Auth is P0 security but commerce is P0 revenue.

changes: ADD COLUMN business_id to products (FK -> businesses.id)
ADD COLUMN business_id to communities (FK -> businesses.id)
Migrate existing products: create a default business per creator user, assign products to it
ADD COLUMN owner_user_id to communities (FK -> users.id) for backward compat
phases.risk: MEDIUM — new tables, existing table alterations
phases.note: This is the foundational migration. Orders, entitlements, courses, campaigns all FK to businesses.

changes: ADD COLUMN product_type to products (text, enum-like)
ADD COLUMN status to products (text, default 'active')
Migrate revenue table data to transactions (or deprecate revenue table)
Change products.price from doublePrecision to integer (price_cents) — BREAKING
phases.risk: HIGH — breaks existing product creation flow
phases.open_question: Float-to-integer price migration: multiply existing prices by 100 and truncate? What about non-USD currencies?

changes: CREATE TABLE courses (with FK to products)
ADD COLUMN slug to communities (text, UNIQUE)
ADD COLUMN privacy to communities (text, default 'public')
ADD COLUMN type to channels (text, default 'text')
ADD COLUMN status to posts (text, default 'published')
phases.risk: LOW — mostly new tables, minor post table additions

changes: Migrate products.category free-text to FK -> categories.id
Add pgEnum declarations for all enum-like text columns
Add missing indexes (user_id on posts, channel_id on channel_messages, etc.)
Add CHECK constraints for rating (1-5), price (>= 0), etc.
Normalize PK strategy: decide serial vs uuid for all tables
Add updated_at columns to tables that need it (posts, products, communities, channels)
Add RLS policies scoped to business_id / user_id

migration_path.note: 20 existing + 25 new = 45 tables in desired state. 7 existing tables get additional columns in migration phases.

open_questions.question: Multi-tenant strategy: is each business a tenant, or is the entire platform single-tenant with business_id as a scope?
open_questions.impact: Determines RLS policy design, data isolation boundaries, and whether businesses can share data

open_questions.question: PK strategy: standardize on serial (integer) or uuid? Current schema uses serial everywhere except notifications (uuid). New tables proposed as uuid.
open_questions.impact: Consistency, URL patterns, external ID exposure, migration complexity

open_questions.question: Price representation: migrate existing doublePrecision to integer (cents)? This is a breaking change for all product-related code.
open_questions.impact: Financial accuracy for commerce stack. Float prices cause rounding errors.

open_questions.question: Revenue table fate: deprecate in favor of transactions table, or keep as a denormalized analytics view?
open_questions.impact: If kept, revenue becomes a materialized view of transactions. If removed, all dashboard queries rewrite against transactions.

open_questions.question: Product type modeling: single products table with type discriminator + extension tables (courses, etc.) vs separate tables per product type?
open_questions.impact: Shared product fields (title, price, image) in one table with type-specific details in extension tables (recommended) vs duplicated columns across N product tables
open_questions.recommendation: Single products table + extension tables. This is the current direction in the migration path.

open_questions.question: Data isolation between CreatorOS and EOS: separate Neon databases or shared database with schema separation?
open_questions.impact: UMH projection layer currently assumes shared Neon. Separate DBs add operational complexity but guarantee isolation.

open_questions.question: Auth migration timing: Clerk migration before or after commerce tables? Auth is P0 security (broken passwords) but commerce is P0 revenue.
open_questions.impact: If auth first: all commerce code uses Clerk from day 1. If commerce first: commerce code must migrate auth later.

open_questions.question: Documents table: keep or remove? Not mentioned in PRD. Appears to be a Replit Agent addition.
open_questions.impact: Low. If kept, it serves as a creator notes/content drafts tool. If removed, simplifies schema.

open_questions.question: Contacts table: keep as standalone CRM or merge into EOS CRM? EOS already has crm_contacts.
open_questions.impact: If merged, creator CRM becomes an EOS feature accessible from CreatorOS. If kept separate, data is duplicated across apps.

strengths: Clean Drizzle ORM schema with proper FK relationships and cascade deletes
Comprehensive relation definitions for ORM query building
Unique constraints on junction tables (saved_posts, followers, conversation_participants, tagged_users)
Type exports for both Select and Insert schemas (40 total)
Self-referential relationships properly modeled (comments threading, DM replies)
weaknesses: No indexes beyond PKs and unique constraints — all table scans on FK lookups
No enum types — all 'type' and 'status' columns are free text with no validation
Mixed PK strategy (serial everywhere except notifications uuid)
doublePrecision for currency amounts (float precision issues)
Denormalized counters (likes, comments, review_count, chat_count, subscriber_count) with no triggers or application-level sync guarantee
Missing email on users table — core for any auth migration
Communities have no owner — can't enforce who manages them
No soft delete (deleted_at) on any table — cascade delete is the only removal strategy
No updated_at on posts, products, or communities — no edit tracking
related_user_image on notifications is denormalized and will go stale
is_edited on direct_messages is nullable boolean (should be NOT NULL default false)
comments.parent_id has no formal FK constraint, only a Drizzle relation definition
schema_quality_assessment.god_file_risk: routes.ts (53KB) and storage.ts (105KB) contain all API logic and data access. Any schema migration will require massive rewrites of these two files. Recommendation: decompose before migrating.
